Miah Abdul Gafur with Abbasuddin Ahmed, Advocates ----- For the Appellants.

Nurul Islam Palan & others  ----- Appellant.

full_judgment:
7. Defence of the defendants, in short, is that the suit is bad for mis-joinder and non-joinder of parties and causes of action and not maintainable in the present form. Partition in respect of 'Kha' schedule of the properties was not maintainable as the same was not ejamali properties of the parties. Jaki Palan was the sisteen annas owner of 'Ka' schedule properties and he died leaving two sons Alim and Kalim and Alim died leaving son Hamid and Kalim died leaving four sons. Alleged Hiba deed by Moslehuddin in favour of Kalim, Harez and Afsar is fraudulent and illegal. The order of deaths given in the plaint and plaintiffs claimed shares are not correct. In the additional written statement the defendant Nos. 1 and 15 claimed that Khalil and Kalarma, son and daughter respectively of Alim pre-deceased their father. Majam Ali transferred his entire property by Heba-bil-ewaz deed dated 12.2.1946 Ext. B in favour of his daughter Alecha Khatoon with delivery of possession to her and the said Alecha Khatoon died leaving her husband defendant No. 15 Siddique and sons and daughter to inherit the same. All the ejmali properties of Kalim and Alim, at Matkabari in Chandpur have now been brought into hotchpotch. 

 14. Learned Advocate for the appellants failed to show anything in support of his contention that the court below should have passed an ex-parse decree instead of a contested decree as done by him as his clients failed to participate in the hearing on the date of peremptory hearing of the suit after remand. As already noticed the contesting defendants filed hazira of witnesses on that day and subsequently filed a petition for time on the ground of engagement of their lawyer. It does not appear from the said order that the learned Advocate moved that petition. Such practice of filing hazira of witnesses on the date of peremptory hearing of the suit and subsequently filing petition for time on the ground of engagement in another court and non-appearance before the court is nothing but professional misconduct on the part of the learned Advocate. In our view, further hearing of the suit after remand is continuation of the original; trial in which the defendants contested the suit by adducing evidence. Therefore, in spite of failure, of the defendants to participate in the further hearing of the suit after remand, the court below had no other option than to pass a contested decree against them. We, therefore, find no merit in the contention that the suit should again be remanded to the trial Court to give an opportunity to the defendant-appellants to adduce evidence in support of their new case made out in their additional written statement.
